Intractable

in-TRAK-tuh-bul -- stress on the second syllable, TRAK. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Intractable is stubborn or hard to control.

The intractable knot in the anchor line took two sailors and a marlinspike a full hour to work loose.

Worked Example

A puppy learns 'sit' in a week. Her older brother, adopted at six years old, has spent four months ignoring the same command, three trainers, and every treat in the house.

The older dog is intractable: stubborn, hard to handle, resistant to being managed at all. The word works just as well for problems as for personalities -- an intractable dispute is one that refuses to be settled no matter who tries.

How Intractable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

stubborn

stubborn: unwilling to change or give way

obstinate

obstinate: stubbornly refusing despite all persuasion

unmanageable

unmanageable: impossible to control or handle

Antonyms

docile

docile: easy to manage, lead, or teach

manageable

manageable: able to be controlled or dealt with

How Strong Is It? — stubborn → intractable → unmanageable

stubborn vs. intractable

stubborn vs. intractable: Stubborn is the everyday word and a shade lighter -- a stubborn child digs in over one bedtime, while an intractable one has defeated every bedtime strategy anybody has ever tried.

unmanageable vs. intractable

unmanageable vs. intractable: Unmanageable states the outcome even more flatly than intractable: an intractable horse fights the reins, while an unmanageable one simply cannot be handled by anyone at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin in-)

root — tract-

root — tract-: to handle, drag, or manage (Latin tractare 'to handle, manage,' from trahere 'to drag')

suffix — -able

suffix — -able: able to be, capable of being (Latin (-abilis))

Put it together

Put it together: This unit's prefix in- ('not') sits on Latin tractare ('to handle, manage'), finished with -able ('able to be') -- read it literally and it says 'not able to be handled.' The same tract- root hauls loads in tractor and traction.

Use the root in a new word: tractor

Use the root in a new word: tractor: The tractor dragged the heavy plow through the thick spring mud.

Root Check

Word Choice

Intractable attaches to two kinds of things: living creatures who will not be handled (an intractable mule, an intractable student) and problems that will not be solved (intractable poverty, an intractable conflict). It is much stronger than 'difficult' -- it says every reasonable attempt has already failed.
